title: A Piece of Cloth
text: Hidden in the Tokyo Midtown garden, two folded steel plates settle on the lawn like dropped cloth. Nothing rises more than 4.8 m. Most of the building lies below.

title: Plaza and Low Wall
text: The west roof folds down from 4.8 m to a knife edge. A concrete wall carries the line on, dividing the paved plaza from the lawn, its steel rail level with the tip.

title: Forecourt
text: Two concrete walls hold a covered outdoor room. Above the glass door, a concrete band and a slot of glass run up to the steel.

title: Lobby
text: The lobby runs along the south glass. The ceiling follows the fold of the roof, from the high back wall down to the glazing.

title: Descent
text: The stair drops beside the sunken court behind 1.1 m glass guards. Daylight follows you down from the side.

title: Gallery 1
text: 133 m², 5 m to the ceiling. Formwork of 1800 × 900 mm and its tie holes set the scale of every wall.

title: Gallery 2
text: 443 m², roughly 15 by 31 m, with a single row of six columns. The room for the large exhibitions.

title: Sunken Court
text: Under the east fold, a full-height glass wall opens to the sunken court. Solid steel mullions, 70 mm wide, carry daylight to the basement.

title: East Tip
text: The east roof folds to within centimetres of the ground. A frosted glass screen stands square to the building, keeping people from the edge.

title: Gallery 3
text: The former café in the west wing, a gallery since 2017. A raking ceiling up to 4.3 m, granite underfoot, the plaza beyond the glass.
